_comment: DISABLED: Ender IO's SAG Mill must not grind a blaze rod back into powder (owner, 2026-08-21,
#280). This file REPLACES enderio:sag_milling/blaze_powder and never loads, so the recipe is
simply absent.
WHY. Ender IO's version returns FOUR blaze powder from one rod. This mod's chain runs the
other way - four powder press into a Blaze Briquette and the Sintering Kiln fires it into one
rod - so the round trip becomes break-even, which is precisely what the Briquette exists to
prevent. CLAUDE.md: it exists because vanilla crafts one rod into TWO powder, so a
one-for-one powder-to-rod recipe would print rods forever.
AND IT IS WORSE THAN BREAK-EVEN, because the SAG Mill multiplies output. Ender IO's own
data_maps/item/grinding_ball.json (read from the 9.0.5-alpha jar the pack pins) runs from
1.0 on the redstone and pulsating balls up to 1.75 on the VIBRANT ALLOY one, with energetic
at 1.6 and end steel at 1.4. So one rod returns up to SEVEN powder against the four it cost:
a 75 percent gain per cycle, automatable, powered, and blaze rods gate brewing here.
That ceiling was first written here as 1.4, because the file was read truncated and only its
first three entries were seen. Caught in review of #281. The conclusion did not change - it
got stronger - but a number stated as measured has to survive being checked.
DISABLED RATHER THAN REBALANCED (owner ruling). Cutting the yield to two would restore the
loss and was the alternative on the table; removing it outright means there is no number to
re-check when Ender IO retunes its grinding balls, and nothing is lost - blaze powder is
already obtainable here by the vanilla route.
HOW A DISABLE WORKS, since there is no remove-recipe primitive. A file at another mod's
recipe id REPLACES it wholesale (only the top file at a path is read), and a condition that
is never satisfied means this replacement itself never loads. Net: the id is gone. The body
below is a valid recipe purely so the file is well-formed; it is never decoded, because a
failing neoforge:conditions stops the rest of the file being read - which is the same
mechanism that lets the AE2 recipes name ae2 items safely when AE2 is absent.
LOAD ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND SILENT. An override at another mod's id only wins if this
mod's datapack is read AFTER theirs, so neoforge.mods.toml carries an optional enderio
dependency with ordering = AFTER. Without it this file is never read, nothing is logged, and
the loop is quietly still there - the same failure as the seventeen NeoForge-reshipped
recipes in #161.
TEMPORARY, like every other cross-mod file here: it is pack content living in the engine
because the pack cannot ship data on 26.1.2, and it leaves with the rest.
